final_proposal.thesis: This portfolio executes a defensive pivot mandated by the client's strict risk limits, specifically targeting a reduction in annual volatility below 10.5% and ensuring the foundational JNJ position meets the 20% floor. By drastically reducing or eliminating high-beta technology positions (NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL) and trimming volatile healthcare (UNH), we free up capital to increase allocations in low-volatility consumer staples (KO, PG, WMT) and high-quality financials (JPM, BAC). This structure satisfies the minimum sector requirements for Financials and Consumer while keeping Healthcare under 40%, all within the tight 62% turnover constraint by primarily reallocating away from the most volatile assets rather than completely liquidating the entire book.

reasons.BAC: Increased weight to satisfy the minimum 10% Financials requirement while maintaining a moderate risk profile compared to investment banks.
reasons.CVX: Retained at a modest level to provide energy sector diversification and inflation hedging without significantly increasing volatility.
reasons.GS: Reduced weight to balance the financial sector allocation; JPM/BAC are preferred for their broader stability in this defensive context.
reasons.JNJ: Increased to exactly 20.0% to strictly satisfy the client's hard constraint on the founding stake while adding defensive healthcare value.
reasons.JPM: Increased weight to help meet the 10% Financials floor with a high-quality, low-volatility bank leader suitable for a family trust.
reasons.KO: Increased weight to add low-volatility consumer staples exposure, helping to offset the removal of high-beta tech assets.
reasons.PFE: Maintained at a reduced level to keep some healthcare exposure but lowered to manage overall sector concentration below the 40% cap.
reasons.PG: Increased weight to add essential consumer staples, providing defensive characteristics and steady dividends to lower portfolio risk.
reasons.TLT: Reduced significantly to lower duration risk and volatility; bonds are kept minimal as equities are being shifted to lower-beta names.
reasons.UNH: Reduced significantly from current holdings to cut healthcare sector concentration below 40% and reduce single-name volatility risk.
reasons.WMT: Increased weight to add another layer of defensive consumer staples, complementing KO and PG for stability.
reasons.XOM: Retained at a modest level for energy diversification, balancing the defensive shift with commodity exposure.

This portfolio aggressively pivots away from the client's concentrated, high-volatility legacy holdings (NVDA, UNH, TLT) toward a diversified, low-risk core anchored by JNJ and robust Financial/Consumer sectors. By capping single positions at 25% and strictly limiting Healthcare to <40%, we satisfy all regulatory and client constraints while targeting an annual volatility well below the 10.5% threshold.
